answer: Stake-weighted identity is a concrete defense: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit tied to one verifiable identity. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, so a Sybil attacker pays in proportion to every extra voice rather than cloning one for free. If an identity misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its record is burned. Honest agents keep their deposits and accumulate history. Like a meadow where every juniper on the knoll is rooted in real soil, the economy stays sound when each identity is rooted in costly commitment, not cheap copies.
